reason: The provided sources contain enough verified facts regarding the sunken Silk Road city of Toru-Aygyr in Lake Issyk-Kul to support a short history script with more than 10 well-sourced claims.
story: High in Kyrgyzstan's Tian Shan mountains, Lake Issyk-Kul conceals a lost chapter of the ancient Silk Road. For centuries, the bustling medieval settlement of Toru-Aygyr thrived along its shores as a vibrant commercial hub where East met West. But at the dawn of the 15th century, catastrophe struck. A massive, violent earthquake shook the region to its core, causing the metropolis to collapse and sink entirely beneath the lake's cold waters. For over six hundred years, its streets, brick buildings, and massive 14-acre Muslim necropolis remained hidden just a few meters deep. Today, underwater archaeologists are rediscovering the site, using advanced drones and diving gear to map its astonishingly well-preserved ruins before wave erosion destroys them forever.
angle: A bustling medieval Silk Road city complete with a massive 14-acre cemetery now sits completely submerged just a few feet underwater in a high-altitude mountain lake after being swallowed by a 15th-century earthquake.

claims.claim: Lake Issyk-Kul is located in eastern Kyrgyzstan in the Tian Shan mountains.

evidence.quote: Issyk-Kul (Russian: Иссык-Куль) or Ysyk-Köl (Kyrgyz: Ысык-Көл [ɯsɯ́q kʰɵl]; lit. 'Hot Lake') is an endorheic saline lake in the western Tian Shan mountains in eastern Kyrgyzstan
Located in northeastern Kyrgyzstan, high in the Tien Shan mountains, the lake sits at an elevation of about 1,607 meters

claims.claim: The lake is the second-largest mountain lake in the world behind Lake Titicaca.

evidence.quote: It is the second-largest mountain lake in the world behind Lake Titicaca in South America.
the second-largest mountain lake in the world after Lake Titicaca.

claims.claim: Archaeologists surveyed submerged ruins in shallow water between 3 and 13 feet deep near the northwest shore of Lake Issyk-Kul.

evidence.quote: The researchers surveyed four submerged sites, between 3 feet and 13 feet (1 and 4 m) deep, near the northwest shore of the lake — the location in the Middle Ages of a mainly Muslim settlement called Toru-Aygyr.

This historic site, officially named the Toru-Aygyr complex, lies just off the northwestern shore of Lake Issyk-Kul, where the Russian Academy of Sciences team dove a surprisingly shallow 3 to 13 feet

claims.claim: The submerged settlement was known as Toru-Aygyr and functioned as a medieval Silk Road trade hub.

evidence.quote: the location in the Middle Ages of a mainly Muslim settlement called Toru-Aygyr.

Underwater explorers recently brought to light the remnants of Toru-Aygyr, a thriving medieval city along the Silk Road that disappeared beneath the surface of this vast Central Asian lake more than six centuries ago.

claims.claim: At the beginning of the 15th century, a terrible earthquake caused the city to go under the waters of the lake.

evidence.quote: At the beginning of the 15th century, as a result of a terrible earthquake, the city went under the waters of the lake
At the beginning of the 15th century, as a result of a terrible earthquake, the city went under the waters of the lake.

claims.claim: Researchers discovered a millstone among fired-brick building remains, indicating a grain mill.

evidence.quote: The team discovered the remains of several now-submerged buildings made with kiln-fired bricks, including one that contained a millstone — evidence that it was once a mill for grain.
What they mapped, the Russian Geographical Society announced, was a medieval city: fired-brick buildings, a stone millstone, big ceramic jars and a Muslim cemetery

claims.claim: An underwater site revealed a Muslim cemetery covering roughly 14 acres.

evidence.quote: One of the underwater sites revealed the remains of a Muslim cemetery that covered an area of roughly 14 acres (6 hectares) — about the size of 11 football fields.
A second zone held the burial ground, an expanse of graves 300 metres by 200, which Live Science works out to about 14 acres, or eleven football fields of dead.

claims.claim: Human remains recovered from the cemetery were found with their faces turned toward Mecca.

evidence.quote: The team recovered the remains of two of the dead from the cemetery, and found that their faces had been turned toward the direction of Mecca, which is now in Saudi Arabia — a common practice in Muslim burials.
Skeletons lie with their faces turned towards the qibla, the direction of the Kaaba in Mecca.

claims.claim: Valery Kolchenko and Maksim Menshikov led the archaeological expedition efforts.

evidence.quote: "The monument under study is a city or a large commercial agglomeration on one of the important sections of the Silk Road," archaeologist Valerii Kolchenko, the head of the Kyrgyzstan contingent of researchers on the expedition...
The work was led by Maxim Menshikov, an underwater archaeologist at the Institute of Archaeology of the Russian Academy of Sciences (IARAS).

claims.claim: Archaeologists also discovered a large intact ceramic vessel known as a khum embedded in the lake sediment.

evidence.quote: Another site in the sunken city yielded several pieces of medieval Muslim pottery, including a large and intact khum, or water jar, that the researchers plan to raise during a future expedition.
Another site uncovered fragments of medieval ceramics along with a large intact khum, a storage vessel used for holding grain, liquids, or other goods.

disputed: Whether residents had completely cleared out before the earthquake struck or if the disaster caught an active population off guard is treated variably by different researchers, and should be attributed or omitted in a script.
